sections.title: Test coverage analysis — cadence-lane-2
sections.content: I verified this against the live repo rather than trusting the (truncated) context or prior session notes — several things in memory turned out to be stale or incomplete once checked. Findings below are grouped by what's actually new/actionable vs. what's already tracked.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Read full source for every module shown only as test excerpts (`UsageIndicator.tsx`, `ranking.ts`, `format.ts`, `ship-format.ts`, `graph-visual.ts`, `design-memory-shared.ts`, `ResearchActivity.tsx`), then grepped the whole `src/` tree for `*.test.ts*` files sitting both beside their source and in a sibling `__tests__/` dir, to get an exhaustive (not sampled) duplicate-suite list.

---

sections.title: 1. Untested functions/classes — the real gap
2. Duplicate test suites — verified exhaustively, larger than tracked
sections.content:
Prior sessions flagged "7 modules" with duplicate suites. A repo-wide scan (matching any `X.test.ts` that exists both beside its source and under a sibling `__tests__/`, plus the differently-named `*-coverage.test.ts` pairs) finds **8**:

| Module | Files | Lines | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat/ResearchActivity` | 4 files | 1735 | Two duplicate **pairs**, not one: `ResearchActivity.test.ts` (906) + `__tests__/ResearchActivity.test.ts` (144) both test the pure functions; `ResearchActivity.test.tsx` (291) + `__tests__/research-activity-dom.test.tsx` (394) both DOM-render the same two components |
| `discover/ranking` | 2 files | 832 + 441 | `ranking.test.ts` is the superset (includes the `nextActionFor` differentiation suite, see §3) |
| `discover/format` | 2 files | 754 + 399 | `format.test.ts` is the superset — `format-coverage.test.ts` never touches `signalPreview`/`signalCleanBody`/`signalHasRaw` (the biggest, most edge-case-heavy chunk of the file) |
| `knowledge/decisions-shared` | 2 files | 86 + 296 | **Not a pure duplicate** — root file tests `ageOf`/`hasSource`/`displayWho`; `__tests__/` file tests `ageOf`/`SOURCE_LABEL`/`STATUS_TONE`. Deleting either loses coverage of exports the other never touches |
| `governance/incident-format` | 2 files | 67 + 205 | `__tests__/` version is the superset |
| `obsidian/graph-slider` | 2 files | 270 + 58 | newly surfaced, not in prior audits |
| `supaprod/Sketch` | 2 files | 313 + 472 | newly surfaced, not in prior audits |
| `lib/nav-model` | 2 files | 187 + 45 | newly surfaced, not in prior audits |

Consolidation recommendation: for the 6 pairs where one file is a strict subset (ranking, format, incident-format, graph-slider, Sketch, nav-model, and both ResearchActivity pairs), keep the larger file and delete the smaller after diffing test names to confirm no unique case is lost. For **`decisions-shared`, do not delete either file as-is** — merge first, since each currently covers exports the other doesn't.

---

sections.title: 3. Doc rot masquerading as a coverage gap
sections.content:
`src/components/discover/ranking.test.ts:601-621` carries a large comment block titled `★ CRITICAL GAP: nextActionFor verdict differentiation`, dated to a 2026-07-09 audit, claiming `nextActionFor` "currently returns 'Draft the spec' for all verdicts except PENDING." I read the live source (`ranking.ts:211-230`): it already differentiates all five verdicts (`SHIP`→"Draft the spec", `WATCH`→"Gather more evidence", `REVISE`→"Address Critic feedback", `KILL`→"Understand why it was rejected", `PENDING`→"Challenge with the Critic first"), and the tests directly below the comment (lines 623-832) assert exactly that and pass. The bug was fixed; the comment describing it as current was not updated. Recommend rewriting that block to state the fix landed and the tests are regression coverage — as written it will mislead the next engineer into re-"fixing" a non-bug.

---

sections.title: 4. Error handling / edge cases
sections.content:
This area is unusually well covered already (malformed-timestamp, non-object-input, and negative/NaN-clamp cases are asserted repeatedly across `format`, `ranking`, `decisions-shared`, `ship-format`). I did not find a genuine missing error-handling test in the modules read. One real edge case remains open in `graph-visual.ts:89` — `resolveKindColors` is tested with a plain `{}` cast to `HTMLElement` (no real `getComputedStyle`), so the `typeof window !== "undefined"` SSR guard's *false* branch (server-side call) is never actually exercised in a non-browser global — worth a dedicated case if the graph is ever rendered in an SSR path.

---

sections.title: 5. Integration test gaps
sections.content:
- **Ink library × real surfaces**: no test anywhere imports from `@/components/ink` — once routes are ported onto it (Phase 2b per your build log), there's no regression net between the unit level and full-page E2E.
- **`ResearchActivityLine`/`ResearchSummaryRow` are tested in isolation only** — always mounted directly with hand-built props, never through the actual chat message stream (`AskPanel`/`chat.ts` SSE → `MessageMeta` → these components). A real SSE-driven integration test would catch a protocol drift (e.g. a backend field rename) that unit tests mounting the components directly cannot.
- **`UsageIndicator` inside `_authenticated.settings.tsx`**: consumed with no test confirming the real `used`/`allowance` values reaching it from the billing data layer match what renders.

---

sections.title: What I did *not* re-flag
sections.content:
`graph-visual.ts`'s `resolveKindColors`/`usePrefersReducedMotion` — listed in a prior session's "modules needing coverage" note — is now thoroughly tested (renderHook, MutationObserver setup/cleanup, SSR guard, reactivity), so I'm treating that as resolved rather than re-reporting it.

**Next step, if you want it:** I can open a PR that (a) adds the Ink + UsageIndicator test files above, (b) fixes the stale ranking.ts comment, and (c) merges the 6 clear-cut duplicate pairs — say the word and I'll start with whichever slice matters most.
